tip: Swedish commands drop the subject: stäng is just the bare verb, no 'du'. Stäng fönstret (Close the window).
Det gör inget is a set phrase for 'it doesn't matter', literally 'it does nothing'.
As an adverb here, lugn takes the neuter -t: lugnt. Ta det lugnt is the fixed phrase for 'take it easy'.
En-words ending in -a form the definite plural with -orna: räka becomes räkorna (the shrimp).
Rasta specifically means to walk or exercise an animal: Han rastar hunden (He walks the dog).
Framme means already there or up ahead at a spot; fram is for motion toward: Övergångsstället är framme.
Regular comparatives add -are: snabb becomes snabbare (faster).
Being in a hurry uses ha, not vara: Jag har bråttom.
Adjectives ending in -er drop that e before -are: vacker becomes vackrare (more beautiful).
Hålla med (agree) is a two-part verb, and inte goes between the parts: Jag håller inte med.
After the modal kan, the next verb is a bare infinitive with no att: Det kan vara sant.
Flyta is a strong verb, so its past is flöt, not flytade: De flöt på vattnet.
Kliva av means to get off a vehicle; av is the particle it needs: Vi klev av bussen.
For vi the reflexive pronoun is oss: dra sig tillbaka becomes Vi drog oss tillbaka (we pulled back).
Ha ont om means to be short of something: Jag har ont om tid (short on time).
Spela roll means to matter, literally 'play a role': Det spelar roll varje dag.
The frame se something som means 'see as': Jag ser det som en möjlighet.
Det går inte att plus a verb means 'you can't' or 'there's no way to': Det går inte att klaga.
Swedish uses vill att plus a clause where English uses an infinitive: vill att vi läser (want us to read).
Start with an adverb and the verb still comes second, before the subject: Självklart kommer jag.
Längta takes efter for the thing you long for: Jag längtar efter sommaren.
Tacka pairs with för to mark what you are grateful for: De tackar dig för hjälpen.
Sjunga is a strong verb, so its past is sjöng, not sjungde: Vi sjöng sånger.
